source: simulcara/situated-evals/experiment_logs/2026-11-20/idea_search.md (ideas #1-#5, wild W1-W2, plus #15 as the card the checker must reject for missing math). Units are CPS skill (dskill ~ d(nats/cell) / 0.74).

analysis.note: noiseFloor = 2 x paired SE ~0.0003 for a KWIDE-sized change (tx_s1 CI half-width 0.0006 over 1449 respondent clusters); headroom = CPS optimistic copy headroom +0.0057 (idea_search #2).

cards.title: Density-matched leave-one-out twin counts (SIM_TWLOO)
cards.model: p_i = (c_i + alpha_{h,b} B_i) / (C_i + alpha_{h,b}), c_i(y) = sum_{j in N_LOO(i)} k_lambda(d_ij - d_i,min) 1{y_j = y}, N_LOO(i) = visible rows except i

lossTerm.why: (M) 5-fold OOF neighbour pools hold 0.8 n_v rows, so alpha is chosen on bucket populations (OOF d>=2 share 0.331) that differ from the hidden ones (0.253); the mismatch biases the trust level

assumptions: each row in bucket b has a copy source with probability tau_b, y_i = y_j with probability rho_h, else y_i ~ B_i
kNN counts have no fitted parameters, so LOO counts are honest
the visible-mate leak (1 dof of ~9k rows x 28 candidates) is negligible
cards.derivation: For a single-neighbour bucket the posterior is p = (1-w) B + w e_{y_j} with w = 1/(1+alpha). Maximising tau log(w + (1-w) b) + (1-tau) log((1-w)(1-b)) gives the first-order condition tau(1-b)/(w + (1-w) b) = (1-tau)/(1-w). Under 5-fold OOF, tau_b^OOF is lowered in the unique buckets by rows whose partner sits in the same fold, so w* is set too small (alpha too large) in near buckets and far buckets learn no update; LOO restores the hidden bucket composition (mean d_min 1.223 vs hidden 1.206).

prediction.statement: the LOO 'buckets vis' histogram matches 'buckets hid' (near-bucket share 50.1% -> ~59% on tx_s1), the OOF twin gain rises above 1.141 nats/row, and the paired CPS delta is > 0; delta <= 0 with both shifts present falsifies the theory

estimation.estimated: (lambda, alpha) per (head, bucket) from the 28-candidate grid, unchanged from TW2; only the neighbour pool changes
estimation.method: argmax of OOF log-lik gain behind the 0.1 nats/row gate
estimation.crossFit: B_oof stays the 5-fold OOF blend; (lambda, alpha) chosen on other folds' rows; strict variant chooses alpha for fold f only from rows whose neighbours lie outside f

expectedGain.derivation: a 0.05 shift in tau at b in {0.3, 0.5} costs 0.011-0.017 nats per affected cell (0.014/0.74 = 0.019 skill); affected cells 10-25% (0.175) of hidden cells on updated heads; 0.019 x 0.175 x 0.75 = 0.0025 (range +0.001 to +0.004)

algorithm.steps: in twin_posterior2 replace the fold loop filling oi/od/om with twin_neighbours(G, vis_idx, vis_idx, w, m=TWIN_M+1) and mask self with idx==arange (exact duplicates tie); same switch for the bucket computation at ~line 1796
algorithm.complexity: O(n_v^2 |G|) over 128-row chunks, same as now; no GPU, no new memory

selfCritique.argument: changes only which visible rows enter the GIVEN-similarity counts; no unit identity is inferred

cards.title: Continuous trust gate instead of bucketed alpha (SIM_TWGATE2)

citations.title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models

cards.model: p_i = (1 - w_i) B_i + w_i c_hat_i, c_hat_i = c_i^lambda / C_i, w_i = sigmoid(eta_h + theta^T phi_i), phi = [d_min, 1{unique}, log(1+n_tied), d2 - d_min, log C_i, max_y c_hat_i(y), H(B_i), log B_i(argmax c_hat_i)]

lossTerm.why: (B, V) 12 buckets x 28 candidates x ~200 heads argmax picks are coarse and carry winner's-curse noise sigma sqrt(2 log M); a smooth low-dimensional gate removes both

assumptions: trust varies smoothly with n_tied, the second-neighbour gap and the prior entropy
theta is shared across heads; per-head intercepts shrink toward 0

estimation.estimated: theta (8-10 shared) and eta_h per head with an L2 penalty
estimation.method: L-BFGS on sum -log p_i(y_ih) (concave in w)
estimation.crossFit: theta^(-f) fitted on folds != f and applied to fold f OOF; hidden rows use theta fitted on all visible rows; on/off by cross-fitted gain >= 0.1 nats/row

expectedGain.derivation: optimistic copy headroom +0.0057 minus GPU-measured TW2 gain +0.0026 leaves ~0.003; a smooth gate recovers a third to a half: 0.003 x 0.42 = 0.00125 (range +0.001 to +0.0015)

algorithm.steps: new twin_gate2(...) replaces the (lambda, alpha) loop in twin_posterior2 when the switch is on; reuses oi/od/om/hi/hd/hm and _twin_counts; third arm combines with TWLOO
algorithm.complexity: H x n_v x |phi| ~ 18M floats (150 MB float64; chunk by head or float32); ~50 L-BFGS iterations, seconds on CPU

prediction.statement: fitted theta > 0 on 1{unique}, gap and consensus, < 0 on log(1+n_tied); theta_gap ~ 0 with paired delta <= 0 means buckets were already sufficient

selfCritique.argument: a smooth trust weight over retrieval features; no pairing decision

cards.title: Empirical-Bayes head-pooled shrinkage of the (lambda, alpha) selection (SIM_TWEB)

citations.title: Stein's Estimation Rule and Its Competitors: An Empirical Bayes Approach

cards.model: c*_hb = argmax_c [ S_hb(c) + kappa n_hb S_bar_b(c) / n_bar_b ], S_bar_b(c) = sum_h S_hb(c) n_hb / sum_h n_hb

lossTerm.why: (V) per-(h, b) argmax over 28 candidates on 25-170 visible rows in buckets 2-5 is selection noise; pooling toward the bucket curve is a James-Stein posterior mode

assumptions: candidate gain curves are exchangeable across heads within a bucket

estimation.crossFit: kappa chosen by the existing fold cross-fitting

expectedGain.derivation: V-only share of the ~0.003 residual: 0.003 x 0.22 = 0.00065 (range +0.0003 to +0.001)

algorithm.steps: precompute S for all heads, then choose c*_hb inside the bucket loop of twin_posterior2 (~15 lines)
algorithm.complexity: O(H x B x 28) after the existing S computation

prediction.statement: the paired delta concentrates in buckets with < 200 rows; concentration in big buckets means noise

selfCritique.argument: pools selection curves across heads; no row-level matching

cards.title: Per-regime pool weights, MoE by twin bucket (SIM_POOLB)
cards.model: p ∝ prod_k p_k^{w_k(r)}, r in {unique-twin near, other}; log-linear pooling is Bayes-optimal when expert evidence is conditionally independent given y

lossTerm.why: (B) TabICL sees the twin row too, so twin evidence is double counted (or diluted) by one weight across regimes

assumptions: twin evidence is shared between the twin-updated blend and TabICL
cards.derivation: For a product of experts with tempered likelihoods the optimal weight on expert k is its share of independent evidence. In the unique-near regime TabICL either copies the twin (redundant evidence) or dilutes it; both give w*_t(unique) < w*_t(other).

prediction.statement: logged per-regime picks show w_t(unique) < w_t(other) for most tasks and paired delta > 0; otherwise T2 is wrong

estimation.estimated: one shared regime offset dw across tasks
estimation.method: grid over dw on the weighting fold
estimation.crossFit: picks on the 20% weighting fold (same selection risk as KWIDE)

expectedGain.derivation: unique-near cells are 29% of CPS rows; PP (-0.00008) says dilution is small: 0.0057 x 0.29 x 0.3 = 0.0005 (range 0 to +0.001)

algorithm.steps: pass the bucket vector (om, hm) from the twin posterior into the per-task TabICL/Kumo weight pick; pick per (task, regime) with a shared offset
algorithm.complexity: 2x the weight picks; negligible compute; needs a GPU paired run

cards.title: Per-head twin metric (SIM_TWMET)
cards.model: d_ij^(h) = sum_g w_g^(h) 1{G_ig != G_jg}, w^(h) in W = {w_knnopt, 1, w_MI(h)}, w_MI(h)_g ∝ MI(G_g; Y_h) normalised to mean 1

lossTerm.why: (B) the instrument-wide knn_opt weights are tuned for kNN accuracy averaged over heads; hours and industry heads may want another distance

assumptions: the best twin distance differs by head
MI weights are estimable from visible rows

estimation.estimated: metric choice per head jointly with (lambda, alpha)
estimation.crossFit: same 5-fold cross-fit; MI computed on training folds

algorithm.steps: compute neighbours under each of 3 metrics in CPU chunks; choose per head with the (lambda, alpha) cross-fit

prediction.statement: hours/industry heads pick a non-default metric and the paired CPS delta is > 0

selfCritique.argument: per-head GIVEN weights on CPS, where rows are not grouped into households

cards.title: Per-head twin metric on ACS (SIM_TWMET, nh_s2)
cards.model: d_ij^(h) = sum_g w_g^(h) 1{G_ig != G_jg}, w^(h) in W = {w_knnopt, 1, w_MI(h)}, w_MI(h)_g ∝ MI(G_g; Y_h) normalised to mean 1

lossTerm.why: (B) the instrument-wide knn_opt weights are tuned for kNN accuracy averaged over heads; hours and industry heads may want another distance

assumptions: the best twin distance differs by head
MI weights are estimable from visible rows

estimation.estimated: metric choice per head jointly with (lambda, alpha)
estimation.crossFit: same 5-fold cross-fit; MI computed on training folds

algorithm.steps: compute neighbours under each of 3 metrics in CPU chunks; choose per head with the (lambda, alpha) cross-fit

prediction.statement: ACS heads pick a non-default distance and nh_s2 improves

selfCritique.argument: GIVEN-similarity kNN, the same class as knn_opt

cards.title: Matrix completion / CF over respondents x items (#15, not recommended)
cards.model: collaborative filtering over respondents and items

lossTerm.why: low-rank structure over respondents and items

expectedGain.derivation: none: a hidden row has no observed PREDICT entries, so this is the side-information model already tried

algorithm.steps: fit inductive MC with GIVEN side information

cards.title: Wild W1: profile density as a twin-trust signal (SIM_TWDENS)
cards.hunch: a rare profile with a unique visible match is far more likely a true copy source than a profile common in the population; split the unique bucket by n_all(i) = #{k != i : d_ik <= d_i,min + 0.05} over visible + hidden GIVEN rows into {1, 2-3, >3}

prediction.statement: on CPS the alpha picked for n_all = 1 is <= 0.3 and for n_all > 3 is >= 3, and the paired delta on tx_s1 is > 0; if the alpha picks do not separate the hunch is dead

selfCritique.argument: counts how crowded a GIVEN profile region is; no pairing decision

cards.title: Wild W2: hidden-hidden twin consensus (SIM_HHC)
cards.hunch: mutual unique near-profile hidden pairs should have near-identical Bayes posteriors but get independently noisy estimates; replace each with the normalised p_i^(1-beta) p_k^beta, beta chosen on visible-visible analogue pairs

prediction.statement: gains only on d >= 2 rows (25% of CPS hidden rows, 37% of the loss) and ~0 elsewhere; OOF analogue picking beta = 0 kills it

ruleRisks.why: treats mutual unique near-profile hidden rows as twins whose posteriors should agree, which is close to same-unit matching

selfCritique.argument: GIVEN similarity among unlabelled rows is the kNN class, but pairing rows for consensus is close to unit classification; idea_search.md flags it for the coordinator

compliance.note: Hard rules for SimulacraBench as ruled by the coordinator on 2026-11-20. nh_s2 is the ACS proxy, where household mates make metric changes sensitive.
